settings.headline: Numbing cream FAQ
settings.subhead: Honest answers to the questions people ask most about cosmetic numbing — what it does, how to use it safely, and when to check with your practitioner.
settings.image_alt: Editorial Senseless numbing range on a warm off-white background

settings.body: Senseless is a UK cosmetic numbing range made for comfort before aesthetic treatments. Numbing reduces discomfort rather than removing it, it's preparation rather than part of the treatment, and your practitioner's guidance always comes first. The answers below cover the questions that come up most.

settings.question: Does numbing cream work?
settings.answer: Topical numbing cream reduces the discomfort of many cosmetic treatments rather than removing it entirely; how noticeable that is depends on the product, the area and how it's applied.

settings.question: What's the difference between the strengths?
settings.answer: Clinical, Advanced and Professional are different strengths of the same range, matched to different treatments — stronger isn't automatically better. The Senseless System helps you choose.

settings.question: Cream, gel or spray — which do I need?
settings.answer: Cream suits broad coverage and most appointments, gel suits precise facial work, spray suits larger or awkward areas. Make your Selection to match it to your treatment.

settings.question: Is numbing cream safe?
settings.answer: Used as directed on healthy, unbroken skin, topical numbing cream is widely used for cosmetic treatments; always follow the product's instructions, patch test first, and check with your practitioner if you have sensitive skin or a skin condition.

settings.question: Should I patch test?
settings.answer: Yes — a patch test on a small area before first use is sensible, especially if your skin is reactive. Follow the product's guidance.

settings.question: Are there side effects?
settings.answer: Some people experience temporary redness or mild irritation at the application site; if you have a reaction or any concern, stop and speak to a professional.

settings.question: Can I use it on broken or irritated skin?
settings.answer: No — apply only to clean, healthy, unbroken skin, and follow the product's instructions.

settings.question: Can I use numbing cream before treatments like microneedling or laser?
settings.answer: Often yes, as preparation for comfort — but many practitioners apply their own as standard and have their own guidance, so always check with yours first.

settings.question: My numbing cream didn't feel like it worked — why?
settings.answer: Comfort varies by product, area, skin and how it's applied; if it didn't suit you, your practitioner can advise on what to use and how. Numbing reduces sensation rather than removing it.

settings.question: Is it a medicine?
settings.answer: No — Senseless is a UK cosmetic product, formulated in the United Kingdom, not a medicine.

settings.body:
• Senseless is a UK cosmetic numbing range, formulated in the United Kingdom — not a medicine.
  • Numbing reduces discomfort; it doesn't remove all sensation.
  • Apply only to clean, healthy skin, patch test, and follow the product's instructions.
  • Many practitioners apply their own numbing — check before your appointment.
